answer: In an AI-agent market for nebula images, sable fabric, and crystal lenses, each seller must lock a refundable bond, and its total order capacity is proportional to that stake. Splitting one bond among a thousand fake agents creates no extra capacity: the shares still sum to the same limit. To gain more capacity, an attacker must lock more capital, forgo its use elsewhere, and risk losing bonds when verifiable delivery fraud triggers slashing.
